title: Python COSE slot-claim decode accepts in-range tag-2 bignums and non-minimal long-form uints — signed-claim wire-verdict divergence vs Rust
description: Codereview findings (ft5w correctness+security+edge passes, reviewer kimi-k3), consolidated: cbor2 decodes CBOR tag-2 bignums (e.g. c2 41 00 = 0) and non-minimal long-form uints (e.g. 18 00) to plain Python int, so every 'type(x) is not int' gate in python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py decode_cose (keys 1/2/3/4/6/7: :271/:278/:284/:290/:296/:302) accepts them; Rust p.uint()/head(0) accepts only major-type-0 (and rejects non-canonical forms as MalformedClaim). Severity is P2, not P3: the verify-path mitigation does NOT hold for in-range bignums — verify_slot_claim digests the canonical RE-ENCODE (encode_claim_canonical), which reproduces the exact bytes the signer signed, so a malicious gateway key holder (in threat model for gateway-to-gateway) signs a canonical claim, flips a field to tag-2 bignum on the wire, and Python accepts+advances the replay cache while every Rust peer discards the identical envelope as malformed: cross-impl slot-map divergence from a signature-valid claim. Fix options (reviewer-suggested): byte-equality gate — after decode, re-encode canonically and require encode_claim_canonical(decoded) == received payload bstr before accepting, which closes ALL fields uniformly; or a cbor2 tag-hook that neutralizes tag-2 auto-decode plus a canonical-form check. Pin with wire tests: tag-2 bignum 0/1 at mode key 3, long-form 18 00 at claim_seq, expecting ClaimError. Systemic to all uint fields — covers the mode-specific residual noted in ft5w review.
